# NodePaint

<!-- Generated from the doc comments in the library. Do not edit this file. -->

What an element paints, captured so the compliance preflight can evaluate colour contrast without a second render pass or any inspection of rendered output.

Colours are "#rrggbb" strings with alpha carried separately, so an opaque document produces no alpha values at all and fixtures stay readable across languages. Elements that paint nothing relevant produce no NodePaint.

Namespace `BonniePDF`.

## Constructors

```csharp
new NodePaint()
```

## Properties

- [`BackdropUnknown`](#backdropunknown): The node paints something behind its children that cannot be reduced to one opaque colour — layers or a freely drawn surface.
- [`Background`](#background): The element's own resolved background fill, "#rrggbb"; null when it has none.
- [`BackgroundAlpha`](#backgroundalpha): Background alpha in [0,1); null when fully opaque.
- [`Bold`](#bold): True when the resolved font weight is 700 or heavier.
- [`FontSize`](#fontsize): Rendered text size in points; null when the element paints no text.
- [`Text`](#text): Resolved text colour, "#rrggbb"; null when the element paints no text.
- [`TextAlpha`](#textalpha): Text alpha in [0,1); null when fully opaque.
- [`TextBackdrop`](#textbackdrop): An opaque backdrop resolved from earlier drawing operations in the same canvas.

### `BackdropUnknown`

```csharp
bool? BackdropUnknown { get; set; }
```

The node paints something behind its children that cannot be reduced to one opaque colour — layers or a freely drawn surface. Descendant text is reported as contrast-unknown rather than measured against a guess.
